oneLiner: A re-orientation dashboard that tells PMs where every project stands the moment they switch back to it.
problem: Product managers juggle multiple projects in parallel and lose 15-30 minutes of context every time they switch, reconstructing the last decision, unresolved blockers, and who is waiting on them. This wasted ramp-up time leads to slow replies, duplicated conversations, and dropped threads.
targetUser: Mid-to-senior product managers at startups or scale-ups who own 2-5 concurrent projects and context-switch multiple times per day.
coreFlow: PM lands on the dashboard and sees all active projects as 'context cards' ranked by staleness and urgency.
PM clicks a project card (or hits the global keyboard shortcut to jump to the project they last touched).
The project view surfaces the three anchors: last decision made (with timestamp and owner), current blockers, and open threads with who is waiting on what.
PM marks items as acknowledged, resolved, or nudged, and optionally writes a one-line 'where I left off' note.
The dashboard updates staleness and priority scores in real time so the next switch is instantly oriented.

screens.name: Dashboard / Project Switcher
screens.purpose: Show all active projects as context cards with last-touched time, decision recency, blocker count, and waiting-on count; allow one-click entry into any project.

screens.name: Project Orientation View
screens.purpose: Present the last decision, active blockers, and a 'who's waiting on what' list for one project, with actions to acknowledge, resolve, or nudge.

screens.name: Focus / Handoff Note
screens.purpose: Let the PM write a short 'where I left off' note when leaving a project, which becomes the first thing they see on return.

screens.name: Integrations and Sources
screens.purpose: Connect Slack, Jira/Linear, GitHub, and calendars so decisions, blockers, and waiting-on items are inferred automatically rather than entered manually.

screens.name: Settings and Priorities
screens.purpose: Configure which projects are tracked, staleness thresholds, notification rules, and which sources feed each project.

outOfScope: Full project management (no sprint planning, backlog grooming, or gantt charts)
Real-time chat or commenting — PMs still respond in their source tools
Team-facing dashboards or reporting for leadership
Mobile native apps (web only for v1)
AI-generated summaries of every thread in v1 — start with decision, blocker, and waiting-on extraction only
Time tracking, invoicing, or billing features
Replacing Slack, Jira, Linear, or Notion — Relay reads from them, it does not replace them
